_doc: Inflation benchmarks for retrospective editions dated in 2012: the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at each cutoff. End-2011 state of the verified 2011 register (China 4%, India's 7% end-of-fiscal-year WPI projection), plus the 2012 current-year targets set earlier (Türkiye 5%, set 10 Dec 2009; Brazil 4.5%, CMN Res. 3,880; Colombia 3%, Board of 25 Nov 2011; Indonesia 4.5%, PMK 143/2010), Canada's renewal of 8 Nov 2011 (the 2006 renewal ran to end-2011), and the changes announced during 2012: China's annual objective (5 Mar), the RBI's end-of-fiscal-year WPI projections from its quarterly reviews (24 Jan, 17 Apr, 31 Jul, 30 Oct), and three framework changes recorded although the value is unchanged, because they replace the row's wording: the FOMC's first explicit longer-run inflation goal (25 Jan), the BoJ's 'price stability goal' (14 Feb) and New Zealand's new Policy Targets Agreement (20 Sep). Thailand's 2012 core-inflation target (Cabinet, 17 Apr 2012) equals 2011's and Korea's 2010–12 target is unchanged; next-period targets announced during 2012 (Korea, Türkiye) are not recorded. Every new source URL was fetched and its quoted text checked; sources are shown only once published; no page names a later year.
note: Three economies had no headline-CPI target: the Federal Reserve's statements refer to the PCE price index (see its row; the benchmark is applied to headline CPI), the RBI's objectives referred to the wholesale price index (the benchmark is the RBI's stated end-of-fiscal-year WPI projection), and the Bank of Thailand targeted core inflation. Benchmarks apply to the headline CPI series used here. Each benchmark is the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at the cutoff; China's is the government's annual CPI objective, announced each March (until then the previous year's applies). Where a range was set, its midpoint is used; for the euro area's ‘below but close to 2%’, 1.9%. Sources are listed only if published on or before the edition’s last eligible day.

US.wording: No numerical inflation target. FOMC projections released 23 Nov 2010: 'projections of this mandate-consistent rate of inflation exhibited a central tendency of 1.6 to 2.0 percent, little changed from June' (PCE). 2.0% headline CPI is this monitor's analytical benchmark.
US.index: PCE price index (FOMC projections); benchmark applied to headline CPI

XM.wording: 'A year-on-year increase in the HICP for the euro area of below 2%' … 'maintain inflation rates close to 2% over the medium term' (below but close to 2%: 1.9% used).

JP.wording: 'Understanding of medium- to long-term price stability', reviewed April 2010: it 'falls in a positive range of 2 percent or lower, and the midpoints of most Policy Board members' understanding are around 1 percent'.

GB.wording: June Budget 2010: 'the independent Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Bank of England will continue to target 2 per cent inflation, as measured by the 12-month increase in the Consumer Prices Index (CPI)'.

CA.wording: Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada, 8 Nov 2011: 'The inflation target will continue to be the 2 per cent mid-point of the 1 to 3 per cent inflation-control range'; the agreement was renewed for another five-year period.

AU.wording: Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 30 Sep 2010: 'keeping consumer price inflation between 2 and 3 per cent, on average, over the cycle' (midpoint 2.5%).
